html:
Sevilla la Nueva, on the north coast of Jamaica, was the first Spanish town on the island, founded in 1509 by Juan de Esquivel under orders from Diego Columbus. Christopher Columbus had been stranded nearby for a year in 1503 and 1504.

The Spanish forced the island's Taino people to work for them, and disease and harsh labour soon destroyed them. Enslaved Africans were brought in their place.

The site was unhealthy, and around 1534 the Spanish moved their capital south to Villa de la Vega, later Spanish Town. Jamaica stayed a quiet cattle and supply colony of Spain until the English invasion of 1655. Archaeologists have dug the ruins of the governor's house and church.
